title: Mata v. Avianca fabricated cases
system: legal research and drafting for federal court filing
organization: United States District Court, Southern District of New York

cells.title: Source
body: Judge P. Kevin Castel issued an Opinion and Order on Sanctions in Mata v. Avianca, Inc., 22-cv-1461, on June 22, 2023.
The order concerned legal submissions that cited non-existent judicial opinions generated by ChatGPT and later submitted to the court.

cells.title: Observed behavior
body: ChatGPT generated case names, citations, quotations, and purported judicial opinions that did not exist. The materials were used in court filings and were later defended after the court and opposing counsel could not locate the cases.
The sanctions order records that the fake opinions included real judges' names and false quotations.

cells.context: Sanctions order description of the submitted opinions
cells.output: Respondents abandoned their responsibilities when they submitted non-existent judicial opinions with fake quotes and citations created by the artificial intelligence tool ChatGPT.

cells.label: Fake opinions identified in the sanctions order

cells.source: Mata v. Avianca, Document 54, order section
cells.output: Respondents shall send via first-class mail a letter individually addressed to each judge falsely identified as the author of the fake opinions.

cells.title: Provenance
body: Primary source: Opinion and Order on Sanctions, Document 54, Mata v. Avianca, Inc., No. 22-cv-1461, Southern District of New York.
The case uses the Justia copy for an accessible text version and the court-hosted PDF copy for preservation.

cells.title: Notes
body: The source artifact is the sanctions order, not the original ChatGPT session.
The order records the court's findings about the fake cases and the conduct of the attorneys and firm.

items: 014. Citation fabrication in legal research product
